subject: History
description: Prithviraj Chauhan, Rana Pratap, Mewar, Rajput-Mughal relations

questions.stem: Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by Muhammad Ghori at which battle?
questions.explanation: First Tarain (1191) — Prithviraj defeated Ghori. Second Tarain (1192) — Ghori returned a year later with fresh forces, defeated and captured Prithviraj. This opened the door to Turkish rule in North India and the Delhi Sultanate (Qutb-ud-din Aibak, 1206). Panipat 1526 (Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi) and Khanwa 1527 (Babur vs Rana Sanga) are later battles.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Maharana Pratap fought the Battle of Haldighati (1576) against the forces of Akbar led by:
questions.explanation: Haldighati — 18 June 1576. Rana Pratap of Mewar vs Mughal forces under Raja Man Singh of Amber and Asaf Khan, deputed by Akbar. The battle was inconclusive; Pratap continued guerrilla resistance till his death in 1597. His horse Chetak died saving him. Todar Mal was Akbar's revenue minister; Birbal his court wit; Jai Singh served Shah Jahan/Aurangzeb.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty of Sambhar-Ajmer had its most famous ruler in:
questions.explanation: Prithviraj III, popularly 'Rai Pithora' (r. 1178–1192), is the most famous Chauhan ruler — defeated at Second Tarain. The court poet Chand Bardai wrote Prithviraj Raso about him. Vigraharaja IV expanded the kingdom a generation earlier; Someshvara was Prithviraj III's father. The capital moved from Sambhar to Ajmer under Ajayaraja II.

questions.stem: The first Rajput king to form a matrimonial alliance with Akbar (1562) by marrying his daughter to the emperor was:
questions.explanation: Raja Bharmal of Amber married his daughter (Harkha Bai / Jodha Bai) to Akbar in 1562, opening the Rajput-Mughal alliance. Their son was Jahangir. Bharmal's grandson Man Singh became Akbar's top Rajput general. Mewar (Udai Singh, then Rana Pratap) stood outside the alliance. Marwar joined much later — Jaswant Singh served Shah Jahan / Aurangzeb.

questions.stem: Chittorgarh Fort, the historical capital of Mewar, is located in which modern state?
questions.explanation: Chittorgarh is in Rajasthan and was the Mewar capital before Udaipur. Famous for three jauhars (mass self-immolations of women): 1303 (Rani Padmini vs Alauddin Khalji), 1535 (vs Bahadur Shah of Gujarat), 1568 (vs Akbar). UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan listing, 2013.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Rana Sanga of Mewar was defeated by Babur at which battle?
questions.explanation: Khanwa — 16 March 1527 — Rana Sanga's Rajput confederacy vs Babur; Babur's second major Indian victory after First Panipat (1526, vs Ibrahim Lodi). Ghaghra (1529) was Babur vs the Afghans of Bengal/Bihar. Chausa (1539) was Humayun's defeat by Sher Shah. Sanga was wounded at Khanwa and died in 1528.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The capital of Mewar was shifted from Chittor to Udaipur by which ruler?
questions.explanation: Udai Singh II founded Udaipur in 1559 after Chittor's fall looked imminent; Akbar captured Chittor in 1568. The city is named after him ('Udai' + 'pur'). Rana Pratap succeeded him in 1572. Amar Singh I, Pratap's son, eventually submitted to Jahangir (treaty of 1615). Landmarks: City Palace, Lake Pichola, Jag Mandir.
